requirements.summary: sudo useradd created datauser (uid=1001), confirmed by id command showing uid=1001(datauser) gid=1001(datauser).

requirements.requirement: /srv/data storage for datauser limited to 100MB, enforced by the filesystem itself (not application-level)
requirements.summary: A 100MB file was created, formatted ext4, and loop-mounted at /srv/data, owned exclusively by datauser (mode 700). Writing 200MB as datauser failed with ENOSPC at ~84-86MB usable capacity (ext4 overhead accounts for the difference from the nominal 100MB), and df confirmed the /dev/loop0 93M filesystem at 100% used. This is a valid filesystem-level enforcement mechanism (dedicated loop-mounted filesystem) rather than an application-level check.

requirements.requirement: Limit persists across remounts and reboots
requirements.summary: A persistent /etc/fstab entry was added for the loop mount. An umount/mount cycle showed the same filesystem, ownership, and permissions restored. A full node restart was then performed: pre-restart boot_id (6ab98831...) and healthy baseline were captured, a backgrounded shutdown -r now returned an immediate acknowledgement, a subsequent poll showed connection refused (node down), and a later poll returned a different boot_id (f4b9c173...), directly evidencing a genuine reboot. Post-restart, /srv/data was shown auto-mounted via fstab with correct ownership, and the ENOSPC write-limit test was repeated successfully, confirming the 100MB filesystem-level limit survived the reboot. The fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots (before_prepare and after_executor) independently corroborate the same boot_id values.

overall_summary: The executor created the datauser account, provisioned /srv/data as a dedicated 100MB loop-mounted ext4 filesystem owned exclusively by datauser, and directly demonstrated filesystem-enforced ENOSPC behavior at the capacity limit both before and after a genuine, verified node restart (boot_id changed and was cross-checked against fixed lifecycle snapshots). Persistence via /etc/fstab was configured and validated through both a remount cycle and a full reboot. All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence, and no unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found.
limitations: The 100MB image yields ~86MB of usable space in the ext4 filesystem due to ext4 metadata/reserved-block overhead; the executor's evidence and report account for this, but it means the enforced usable limit is somewhat below the literal 100MB figure named in the task.

Enforcement was achieved via a dedicated loop-mounted filesystem exclusively owned by datauser rather than per-user quota tooling (quotaon/edquota) on a shared filesystem; this is a reasonable alternative implementation but differs from what might be assumed by 'quota enforced by the filesystem.'

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to task purposes: account creation (cmd-29f5467d01134735), filesystem provisioning (cmd-ff40f8a9f0fb4516, cmd-2d7493c38bea4a01), persistence configuration (cmd-d0fb6021307645fc), and bounded verification writes that were promptly cleaned up (cmd-d77024ac0df14644 removed via cmd-60be85ffe3db4d00; cmd-fe5f7e425ed64aac's verify file removed within the same command). The one failed early attempt (cmd-602297a4d0174dec, permission denied) made no state changes and required no reversal. The reboot (cmd-1c0cab6b7f924dee) was a necessary, evidence-supported action directly tied to demonstrating restart persistence. No abandoned files, conflicting services, unsafe exposure, or damaged package state were observed; failed-services and package-health snapshots are unchanged and clean between before_prepare and after_executor.
